minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted a special permit for dimensional variation at 41 Country Road after the earlier permit lapsed.
minutes.summary: The board heard one case from SNR Construction Concepts, whose predecessor's special permit was treated by the building inspector as expired although the well, septic and foundation work were in. After questions about the timeline and the prior owner, a motion to approve was made and seconded, and the chair announced the permit granted with standard conditions. Two July cases were previewed before adjournment.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit for dimensional variation at 41 Country Road, construction having started before the prior permit expired.

decisions.decision: Chair announced the special permit granted, contingent on compliance with all applicable licenses, regulations and laws, and it must be recorded at the registry of deeds before taking effect.
Two cases noted for July: a ground-mount solar request and a garage on Peninsula Drive needing a special permit for dimensional variation.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit for dimensional variation at 41 Country Road, after the earlier permit was treated as expired.
The vote on the motion to approve was not audible in the recording, so the minutes record the chair's announcement of the grant, not a tally.
The grant is contingent on compliance with all applicable licenses, regulations and laws, and it must be recorded at the registry of deeds to take effect.
The applicant, SNR Construction Concepts, said work had begun before the prior permit lapsed; the board questioned the timeline and the prior owner.
Two cases were noted for July: a ground-mount solar request and a garage on Peninsula Drive needing a special permit for dimensional variation.

why_it_matters: For neighbors of 41 Country Road, the permit lets construction continue on a lot that had a lapsed approval, and it takes effect only once recorded at the registry of deeds.
Because the vote itself cannot be heard, a resident who needs the count would have to ask the town for the board's written decision.
